title: The design step is staffed between Gate 1 and the plan, and is skippable
description:
SPIDR child 2 of task-8a6d6660c31c4e119f962d13e6f1505d (architect-20a6d1eb, 2026-09-05). dependsOn child 1 task-5e90317e80ac4b86a9704b6b8ba8874a for the kinds and aggregate.

WHAT THIS ROW OWNS: the LOOP change. The affordance surface offers a design step after Gate 1 and before decomposition; the wrapper staffs a design seat with a mission that reads the approved contract and the PRD; the compiler mission then carries the design ref and its section headings; node missions cite the screens/entities they implement; and a per-goal toggle skips the whole step. No UI - that is child 3.

MEASURED AT HEAD (branch moe/work-2026-09-04) by architect-20a6d1eb:
- The compiler seat plans straight from the approved contract today: `apps/daemon/src/orchestrator/agent-mission-text.ts` `compilerMission` (:78) tells the seat to read `product_contract_read` and the paged PRD and submit the decomposition. There is no design in the chain.
- The affordance surface composes steps in `apps/daemon/src/http/affordance-read.ts`; a new step kind joins that composition.
- The wrapper staffs any READY unclaimed step up to maxAgents (`agent-wrapper.ts:339-372`), skipping HUMAN_ONLY_STEPS (:351) and `session.*` kinds, ordering `node.deliver` first (:348-357) - a design step must fall out of that ordering sensibly rather than competing with node work.

THE SKIP TOGGLE IS A SAFETY VALVE, not a nicety: the parent's DoD 4 requires that a goal can plan WITHOUT a design so the loop never blocks on this step. Build it as a per-goal setting read at surface-composition time, and make the compiler mission STATE that no design exists when it is skipped - a seat that silently gets no design cannot tell the difference between 'skipped' and 'the read failed'.

CONCURRENT EDITOR: task-f79d38b119984ae1ae51eba887a28b7d is rewriting the compiler mission sentence in agent-mission-text.ts under the owner's fence-lift ruling, and task-2c016c04dedc4eb88982a1d8d5108ddf is adding a rejection sentence to the instructions that flow into it. Expect a rebase there and do not delete either row's sentence to make yours fit.
definitionOfDone: The affordance surface offers a design step for a goal whose Gate 1 contract is APPROVED and whose decomposition has not run, and stops offering it once a design exists. Assert both transitions against a real store, and assert the step is ABSENT before Gate 1 approval - a design step offered on an unapproved contract would staff a seat with nothing to design against.

The wrapper staffs the design seat: a surface offering a READY unclaimed design step produces a spawn, asserted by work-item id. Assert its ordering relative to node.deliver is deliberate (agent-wrapper.ts:348-357 currently ranks node.deliver first) and say in a step note which rank you chose and why.

The design seat's mission reads the approved contract and the PRD and names the five sections it must submit - assert the produced mission text contains the section headings, so a seat cannot be staffed with an underspecified brief.

AFTER a design exists, the compiler mission bytes contain the design REF and the five section headings - assert on the produced mission text (the parent's DoD 2). This is the clause that makes the design load-bearing rather than decorative: a design nothing reads is a form nobody fills in twice.
Node missions cite the screens/entities they implement, drawn from the design - assert one node mission names a screen from the design it was compiled against.

THE SKIP TOGGLE: a per-goal 'plan without a design' setting makes the surface skip the design step entirely and the decomposition run opens with no design; the compiler mission STATES that no design exists rather than silently omitting it. Assert the mission text says so - the difference between 'skipped' and 'unreadable' must be visible to the seat.
Gates quoted with their `Test Files N passed` count lines: `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test`, `pnpm typecheck`.
taskRails: NO UI. The Design tab, the version on the plan-approval card, the live drive and the docs are child 3's.
THE LOOP MUST NEVER BLOCK ON THIS STEP. The skip toggle is a required safety valve, not an optional extra; a goal must always be able to reach a plan.
A SKIPPED DESIGN IS STATED, NOT OMITTED. A seat that receives no design section cannot distinguish a skipped step from a failed read, and will guess.
agent-mission-text.ts has two other rows editing it concurrently (task-f79d38b1's fence-lift rewrite and task-2c016c04's rejection sentence). Rebase, do not delete their sentences.
FEATURES ONLY (inherited): no security-boundary or policy work.

implementationPlan.description: MAKE THE DESIGN LOAD-BEARING. Same two files. THREE OUTCOMES, and the third is the one that matters: a design EXISTS -> the mission carries its REF and the five section headings; the goal is marked SKIPPED -> the mission STATES that no design exists BECAUSE THE STEP WAS SKIPPED; no design and no marker -> say that too. A seat that simply receives no design section cannot tell 'skipped' from 'the read failed' and will guess - that is what taskRail 3 forbids. (2) `codeMission` (:48) cites the screens/entities the node implements, drawn from the design. Its `brief: NodeMission` parameter is typed in agent-wrapper.ts, so widening it touches step 4's file - decide there whether the field goes on NodeMission or is passed as its own parameter, and prefer the separate parameter, because agent-wrapper.ts has only six lines of headroom. (3) TESTS, asserting on the PRODUCED MISSION TEXT, not on a helper that rebuilds it: the compiler mission contains the design ref and all five headings when a design exists; it contains an explicit skipped statement when the marker is set; and one node mission names a screen from the design it was compiled against. THE SHAPE THAT MAKES THE GUESS IMPOSSIBLE. `export type DesignBrief` is a three-variant discriminated union — PRESENT {ref, screens, entities} | SKIPPED {reason} | ABSENT. The skip is its OWN VARIANT rather than an absent ref, so THERE IS NO VALUE OF THIS TYPE THAT MEANS "no design" AMBIGUOUSLY. That is the structural half of taskRail 3; the sentences are the other half. SKIPPED mirrors the durable `DesignSkip` marker (design-contracts.ts:122, task-365e5d97's) and carries the operator's reason for the same purpose the marker bounds it, rather than re-deciding what a skip is.

THE THREE COMPILER SENTENCES, verbatim (DoD 6 asks for exactly these):
- PRESENT: `A DESIGN EXISTS for this goal, submitted under design ref "<ref>". Read it with design_read, payload {"goalRef": "..."} and nothing else: it answers the five sections apiSurface, componentList, dataModel, nonFunctional, screens plus openDecisions. Plan the decomposition FROM it - every screen and entity it draws must be implemented by some node, and each node's objective names the screens and entities that node implements.`
- SKIPPED: `NO DESIGN EXISTS for this goal BECAUSE THE DESIGN STEP WAS SKIPPED: the operator declared that this goal plans without one, stating "<reason>". This is a decision, not a missing read - plan from the approved contract and the PRD alone, and do not wait for a design that is never coming.`
- ABSENT: `NO DESIGN ACCOMPANIES THIS BRIEF, and the operator has not declared that it plans without one. Plan from the approved contract and the PRD alone; if one was submitted after you were staffed, design_read with payload {"goalRef": "..."} answers it.`
The section names are interpolated from DESIGN_SECTION_KEYS, not retyped. The ABSENT branch names design_read so an absent design is a recoverable state for the seat rather than a dead end.

WORDING WAS CHOSEN SO THE ARMS CANNOT BE VACUOUS. "This is a decision, not a missing read" appears ONLY in the SKIPPED branch and is the sentence a seat reads to know it must not wait. The ABSENT branch contains NO form of the word "skip", which is what lets the anti-vacuity arm assert `expect(absent).not.toContain("skipped")` at all — had I written the natural "the step was not marked skipped" there, that assertion would have been unsatisfiable and the collapse drill would have had nothing to detect.

THE ANTI-VACUITY ARM (this is the one that makes step 5's drill (i) bite). Beyond the three positive arms there is a fourth that pins MUTUAL DISTINGUISHABILITY: `expect(new Set([present, skipped, absent]).size).toBe(3)` plus seven cross `not.toContain` assertions on meaning-bearing phrases. A test that only asserted "the skipped text contains X" would survive a collapse if X were short enough to appear in both; the set-size arm cannot, because collapsing any two branches makes the set size 2.

NULL IS NOT A FOURTH OUTCOME, AND THE TWO LANES DIFFER DELIBERATELY.
- compilerMission: `null` === ABSENT, asserted with `expect(decomposition(null)).toBe(decomposition({outcome:"ABSENT"}))`. An omitted paragraph is exactly the ambiguity the type exists to remove, so the unwired caller gets the stated ABSENT paragraph.
- codeMission: `null` emits NOTHING, and that asymmetry is deliberate and asserted (`expect(node(null)).not.toContain("design")`). A node step's aggregate is a nodeRef and the wrapper cannot resolve it back to a goal, so a null there means the caller KNOWS NOTHING — and a claim about the design would be worse than silence. An EXPLICIT ABSENT is still stated out loud in that lane too.
The `not.toContain("design"/"Design")` arm was only writable because I checked first that neither codeMission's existing bytes nor `agentRoleForWorkspace(...).fileInstructions` contain the word (`grep -n -i design apps/daemon/src/orchestrator/agent-role-contract.ts` -> no match).

WHICH COMPILER ARM GETS THE PARAGRAPH — a deliberate choice, not an oversight. Only the DECOMPOSITION arm. A design is submitted AFTER Gate 1 approves a contract, so `product_contract.propose_revision` runs at a moment when no design can exist and a paragraph about one there would be noise the seat has to discount. PROVEN, not asserted: see the probe below.

implementationPlan.note:
STAFF THE SEAT. Tests first, RED observed, and the RED ITSELF ANSWERS THE STEP'S FIRST QUESTION.

(1) THE WRAPPER NEEDED NO STAFFING CHANGE — VERIFIED, NOT ASSUMED, AND THE TEST RUN IS THE PROOF. Before touching agent-wrapper.ts I ran the four new arms against the UNCHANGED wrapper: `Tests 2 failed | 2 passed | 46 skipped (50)`. THE TWO THAT PASSED were "staffs a READY unclaimed design step, named by its work-item id" and "dedupes a design step across two passes rather than staffing it twice". So a design step offered READY and unclaimed already staffs, already mints identity under the agent's own credential, already claims durably, and already goes THROUGH the `workItemIdFor` dedupe at the top of the loop rather than around it — with zero lines of new staffing code. The plan's central measurement holds exactly as written. THE TWO THAT FAILED were the mission-dispatch arm and the ordering arm, which are the only two genuine changes this step makes. I added no code that was not needed.

(2) THE RANK I CHOSE, AND WHY — the sentence DoD-2 asks for.
  0. node.deliver   1. design.submit   2. everything else   3. goal.close
I ranked `design.submit` at 1: AHEAD of all generic work, still BEHIND in-flight node delivery. The reason is leverage, not preference. A design GATES THE WHOLE DECOMPOSITION BEHIND IT — while the design rung is unstaffed the goal offers no `planning.submit_decomposition` at all (affordance-planning-offers.ts:178-181 makes the two mutually exclusive), so every node that goal will ever have is waiting on that one seat.
